Subject: MAP: evaluation sprint — observation roster & success test catalog

Alex / Sara —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, we want to make the evaluation as lightweight and reproducible as possible so your stakeholders can sign off quickly. I put together a short observation roster (attached) and a catalogue of small acceptance tests we expect to run during the two-week evaluation sprint. High level goals:

- Validate integration viability (API auth, payload shape, latency under 95th pct SLA)
- Confirm quality on key prompts (clinical note extraction + reranking)
- Surface any data retention / logs questions for procurement

Can you confirm who on Veridian will own the observational checks (user story owner) and which environment we should hit (staging vs. sandbox)? Suggested next steps:

1) You confirm owners and a sandbox endpoint by Thursday EOD (Aug 6).
2) We kick the MAP with a short sync — 30 minutes — on Friday to assign tasks.
3) Execution: 10-day observation window, with a 2-day decision buffer for signoff.

I've attached: MAP_observation_roster_v1.xlsx (roster + task owners) and eval-smoke-scripts.md (short scripts we run).

Rishi

Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: evaluation sprint — observation roster & success test catalog

Alex / team —

Great, thanks for confirming owners and the staging endpoint. Attached is a condensed acceptance-test catalog (we also pasted the table below for quick reference). The goal here is to make each acceptance test executable in ~10–15 minutes so your PMs can run them during the observation window.

Acceptance-test catalog (condensed):

1) Prompt: Extract discharge diagnosis from free-text note
   - Metric: Exact-match on ICD-10 code set (top-1)
   - Threshold: >= 0.92 recall on sample set (n=200)
   - Test owner: Alex Park
   - How to run: POST /v1/generate -> compare structured output to gold sheet

2) Prompt: Flag potential PHI redaction misses
   - Metric: False-negative rate for PHI entity types
   - Threshold: <= 0.03 FN rate on curated sample (n=150)
   - Test owner: Sara Jenkins
   - How to run: run script eval-smoke-scripts.md::phi_check

3) Prompt: Rerank suggestions for medication reconciliation
   - Metric: MRR improvement vs baseline model
   - Threshold: +0.08 MRR over baseline in 500-query smoke set
   - Test owner: Alex Park

4) Operational: 95th percentile latency under 350ms for 512-token requests
   - Metric: P95 latency sampled over 1,000 calls
   - Threshold: P95 < 350ms
   - Test owner: Ben Carter

If any threshold needs to move given the data characteristics you have, flag it in the spreadsheet and we'll review. For the sync: I sent a 10:30am invite for Friday (30m). Agenda: owners + quick runbook, run order for tests, where results land (shared Drive).

Attachments: MAP_observation_roster_v1.xlsx (roster), eval-smoke-scripts.md (scripts).

Rishi

From: Alex Park <alex.park@veridianhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@veridianhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2026 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: evaluation sprint — observation roster & success test catalog

On Fri, Aug 6, 2026 at 08:47, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> If any threshold needs to move given the data characteristics you have, flag it in the spreadsheet and we'll review.

We reviewed the sample sets this morning. Two quick updates:

- PHI check: our curated PHI set contains a higher proportion of edge cases (handwritten notes, OCR noise). Can we relax threshold to <= 0.05 FN for the pilot and then re-evaluate in a follow-up sprint? We flagged the change in the attached roster (column: suggested_threshold).
- Latency: staging sits behind our internal proxy which adds ~40ms. We'll account for that; suggested target for staging is P95 < 400ms with the production cutover still expected to be <350ms.

Otherwise this looks good. We'll run the three smoke tests and post results to the shared Drive folder (link below) by Aug 18 EOD.

Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPdocs

Thanks — Alex
